description: Support disabling workflow profiles per-project (end-to-end) and fix the Settings > Workflows tab display issues (real stages, Settings Search registration, base-ui Select, base-ui Switch toggle).

tasks.title: Server: per-project workflow profile enable/disable backend
tasks.description: Add the disabled-profile blacklist to ProjectWorkflowProfile (JSON column + EF migration AddDisabledWorkflowProfileIds), make the discovery endpoints (/api/workflow-templates/system, /api/workflow-profiles) project-scoped via an optional ?project=<ref> query param that filters out disabled profiles, change EffectiveWorkflowProfileResolver.ResolveCore to return string? and skip disabled profiles in the cascade (null = no enabled profile), add project-scoped toggle endpoints (disable/enable) with the last-enabled invariant, and add the issue-create pre-flight check that rejects creation when the project has zero enabled profiles. This delivers the full server-side enable/disable capability at the API boundary.
acceptanceCriteria: ProjectWorkflowProfileRow has a DisabledWorkflowProfileIds JSON column defaulting to an empty array; EF Core migration AddDisabledWorkflowProfileIds applies cleanly and the system auto-migrates on startup.

GET /api/workflow-templates/system?project=<ref> and GET /api/workflow-profiles?project=<ref> exclude every profile id on the target project's blacklist; omitting the param returns the full unfiltered catalog (backward compat).

POST /api/projects/{projectRef}/workflow-profile/disable adds the profile to the blacklist; POST .../enable removes it. Disabling the last enabled profile is rejected with 400 and error code last_enabled_workflow_profile, and the blacklist is left unchanged.

EffectiveWorkflowProfileResolver.ResolveCore returns string?, skipping any profile on the disabled blacklist across issue-custom -> project-default -> first-enabled-system steps, returning null when no profile is enabled. Read paths (IssueQuerier, IssueGrain.StartAsync) treat null as mohist/local for display safety.

Issue create handler (IssueRoutes.Crud.cs) resolves the effective profile before persisting; returns 400 no_enabled_workflow_profile when the project has zero enabled profiles, and returns 400 unknown_workflow_profile when an explicitly-supplied profile id is on the blacklist. No issue is persisted in either case.
mohist/local is not specially protected: it can be disabled like any other system profile when at least one other profile stays enabled.

Server unit/integration tests cover: blacklist default-empty, endpoint filtering by project, last-enabled disable rejection, resolution cascade skip + null return, and create-path rejection for zero-enabled and disabled-explicit-id. npm test (dotnet build with TreatWarningsAsErrors) passes.
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/ updated (ProjectWorkflowProfileRow, migration, ProjectWorkflowProfileManager, SystemRoutes, ProjectRoutes, EffectiveWorkflowProfileResolver, IssueRoutes.Crud) + accompanying tests
tasks.notes: Design decisions D1-D5. Resolver is public static referenced by IssueGrain and IssueQuerier (all internal) — update all call sites in this task. The ?project= param accepts ref (name-or-id) resolved via ProjectResolver.

tasks.title: CLI: project-scoped workflow list + skill fallback wording
tasks.description: Add --project/--project-id options to `mo workflow list` (reusing the shared option description), resolve the project via ResolveProjectIdAsync, and pass the resolved id as the ?project= query param to /api/workflow-profiles (described) and /api/workflow-templates/system (plain) so the output honors the project's enabled set. Update the bundled mohist-create-issue SKILL.md so the fallback wording is 'the first enabled profile, else fail with an actionable error' and no longer states mohist/local is an unconditional fallback.
acceptanceCriteria: `mo workflow list --described --project <ref>` resolves the project and calls the filtered discovery endpoint; the output excludes every profile the project has disabled and lists every enabled system profile.
When no project is resolvable and --described is set, the command falls back to the unfiltered endpoint with a stderr note (degraded-path safety net).

mohist-create-issue/SKILL.md describes the fallback as 'the first enabled profile, else fail with an actionable error' and contains no statement that mohist/local is guaranteed to exist or is an unconditional fallback.
CLI unit tests cover project resolution + filtered endpoint invocation; skill data change is verified. dotnet build (TreatWarningsAsErrors) passes.
tasks.notes: Design decision D8. Reuses the shared --project/--project-id option description already in MohistCliCommands.cs.

tasks.title: Web: Workflows tab display fixes (real stages + Settings Search)
tasks.description: Replace the hardcoded DEFAULT_WORKFLOW_STAGES chip set in WorkflowProfilesSection.tsx with the profile's real profile.stages from profile detail, and populate the WORKFLOW_DESCRIPTORS array so Settings Search returns workflow-related entries that navigate to the Workflows tab. These are independent display/discoverability fixes with no dependency on the enable/disable feature.
acceptanceCriteria: Each profile card on Settings > Workflows renders the stages from that profile's profile.stages; no card renders a hardcoded ['plan','build','check','integrate'] set that does not match the profile.
Two profile cards whose profile.stages differ render distinct stage chip sets.

WORKFLOW_DESCRIPTORS is populated with at least one entry; Settings Search for 'workflow' returns workflow-related entries that navigate to the Workflows tab, and the registry is no longer an empty array.
npm run typecheck -w packages/web and npm run test:run -w packages/web pass.
tasks.notes: Covers the 'bundled display issues' for stages and Settings Search. No server dependency — real stages come from the existing profile-detail data.

tasks.title: Web: per-profile enable/disable Switch + base-ui Select default control
tasks.description: Create a base-ui Switch primitive (packages/web/src/shared/ui/components/switch.tsx wrapping @base-ui/react/switch with aria-label), make useWorkflowProfiles/getWorkflowProfiles project-scoped (pass ?project=<id>, add project id to the query key, drop the hardcoded mohist/local fallback in useEffectiveDefaultWorkflowProfile), add a per-card Switch toggle that writes the project's disabled-profile blacklist via the toggle endpoints with inline last-enabled blocking, and replace the native <select> in ProjectDefaultWorkflowControl with the project's base-ui Select primitive with disabled-item visual distinction and an amber warning when the current default points at a disabled profile.
acceptanceCriteria: packages/web/src/shared/ui/components/switch.tsx exists, wraps @base-ui/react/switch, and supports an aria-label prop.

useWorkflowProfiles and getWorkflowProfiles pass ?project=<current project id> from useProject(); the query key includes the project id so toggling invalidates the correct cache slice; useEffectiveDefaultWorkflowProfile reports source:'none' when the filtered list is empty (no hardcoded mohist/local fallback).

Each profile card exposes a base-ui Switch (not a hand-rolled toggle) carrying an aria-label describing the profile it controls; toggling it updates the project's disabled-profile blacklist via the toggle endpoints and reflects the new state.
Toggling off the only remaining enabled profile is blocked inline with a clear consequence message; the profile remains enabled and the blacklist is unchanged.

ProjectDefaultWorkflowControl uses the project's base-ui Select primitive (not a native <select>); disabled items in the dropdown are visually distinct (greyed/disabled); an amber warning is shown when the current project default points at a disabled profile.
npm run typecheck -w packages/web and npm run test:run -w packages/web pass.
tasks.notes: Design decisions D6 (Switch primitive) and D7 (project-scoped hook). Depends on T-001 for the toggle endpoints and ?project= filtering; depends on T-003 to serialize WorkflowProfilesSection.tsx edits (T-003 already renders real stages, so this task layers the Switch on top).
